# Public methodology variants

Use these lenses only for the identified gap. They introduce no installed tool,
workshop requirement or authority to choose architecture. The source URLs below
identify the inspected methodologies, not active Codex capabilities.

## Examples and outstanding questions

[Cucumber Example Mapping](https://cucumber.io/docs/bdd/example-mapping/) links
a bounded story to rules, concrete examples and unresolved questions. Keep a new
story outside the agreed boundary unless its owner adds it. A session timebox can
end the conversation while questions remain; route them rather than declaring
completion. Cards, colors, Gherkin and a Cucumber installation are unnecessary.

## Stakeholder quality priorities

[SEI QAW](https://www.sei.cmu.edu/library/quality-attribute-workshop-collection/)
starts from mission concerns and real stakeholder perspectives before architecture
is settled. Consolidate overlapping scenarios without losing conflicting needs;
ask accountable people to prioritize, then refine consequential scenarios. Agent
ratings cannot replace stakeholder votes. Record tradeoffs and owners without
running an architecture workshop or choosing a design.

## Runtime and change quality

[arc42 quality scenarios](https://docs.arc42.org/section-10/) distinguish runtime
responses from the consequences of changing a system or its environment. For
either, name the initiating condition, context, desired response and meaningful
measure when known. An adequate short description needs no longer template.
Leave unsupported targets open; the whole architecture template stays downstream.

## Process perspectives

[EventStorming](https://www.eventstorming.com/) offers organizational improvement,
ecosystem exploration, service exploration and software design perspectives.
Choose the first three only when cross-system stories or conflicting perspectives
obscure intent. Ask real participants about their events and boundaries; label
agent-generated timelines provisional. Software/event-model design remains a
specialist activity. None of these perspectives implies microservices.

## BMAD comparison boundaries

[Forge Idea](https://github.com/bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD/blob/main/skills/bmad-forge-idea/SKILL.md)
separates clarifying meaning, challenging a central claim and improving an open
choice. Preserve that selected stance. Its attack/defend overlay is opt-in;
argument is not stakeholder evidence. Retain settled choices on resume. A clearer
idea or a rejected premise can be a valid outcome; do not force implementation.
Do not import its personas, configuration, memory scripts or HTML reporting.
Its repository-truth rule establishes observed state, not desired owner intent.

[Advanced Elicitation](https://github.com/bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD/blob/main/skills/bmad-advanced-elicitation/SKILL.md)
is a critique checkpoint for existing work. Its catalogue/menu, sequential
refinements and apply/reject lifecycle remain excluded from the shared entry.
The catalogue's individual techniques are not claimed implemented. Proposed
changes still require an actual owner decision where consequential.
